Recommendations from the stakeholders and from geotechnical investigation will be considered. Temporary access roads will be constructed as required for moving heavy equipment and transporting pipe as allowed by landowners and stakeholders. Page 16 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 10.4 SURVEY A topographic survey shall be performed by a Registered Professional Land Surveyor (RPLS) to determine natural and man‐made physical features and site drainage patterns of the property. Topographic survey shall include as a minimum property lines, contours, vegetation, existing structures above and below ground including power poles, power line, pipelines, utilities, roads, culvert, ditches, and fences and inverts of roadside ditches within the property. In addition, topographic survey should include culverts, roads, utilities, or any other features adjacent to the property that may impact the design of the facility. Topographic survey shall identify road names, North arrow and description of benchmarks used for the survey. The Pipeline Environmental Services contractor(s) shall perform all requisite surveys to support acquisition of required permits. Data from these surveys and permits including delineations, seasonal limitations, restoration/revegetation, shall be communicated to the engineer and incorporated in the construction drawings. 11 ELECTRICAL & INSTRUMENTATION Electrical design will be based on NEC 70, NEMA, ANSI and IEEE requirements. Each actuated MLV site with commercial utility service will have a pole mounted transformer (supplied by the utility) with fused cut‐out to accommodate the electrical loads. The actuated and instrumented MLV sites will utilize outdoor equipment, mounted on a switch‐rack. Electrical requirements within the scope of the pipeline design will not exceed low voltage e.g., 480 VAC three phase for larger valve actuators. Smaller actuators may be powered by single phase or split phase AC. Standby power will be considered for critical (e.g., HCA) valve locations. Local solar power generation and storage will be considered for MLV sites remote from available utility supply. Solar shall be considered for facilities with monitoring instrumentation but no additional loads. Rectifiers shall be located at planned pipeline facilities with available utility power where possible. In the event rectifiers must be located separate from planned facilities, consideration shall be given to utility power availability when determining locations. 11.1 AREA CLASSIFICATION The product stream is not hazardous and therefore hazardous electrical area classification around the launchers, receivers, and mainline valves will not be required. If fuel for backup generation introduces hazardous area concerns, area classification will be evaluated at that time. 11.2 POWER SYSTEMS STUDY During the Detailed Design phase, a study will be performed to set design requirements for mainline valve sites.
